Nanny O’Dear kept her on schedule, though the busy plans sometimes became confusing. One night, Ernestine looked pale, and her father suggested face-painting lessons. Ernestine often watched Hugo play as she traveled to class. One day, his ball flew over the fence and landed in her tuba. She wanted to bounce it back, but Nanny reminded her about tuba lessons. That night, Ernestine thought about Hugo’s free play and made a plan. The next day, she left for the park instead of yodeling or knitting. On a hill, she and Nanny enjoyed the view, imagined shapes in clouds, pretended to be bugs and pioneers, and made a daisy crown. When Ernestine missed yodeling, her parents searched the classes for her and finally guessed she might be at water ballet.

video_title: 'Henry Holton Takes the Ice' read by Ray Romano

summaries.summary: Henry Holton comes from a family that loves hockey. Everyone plays, except Grandma, who once won hockey awards before hurting her hip. Henry can skate very well, but he cannot use a hockey stick. He also dislikes skating straight up and down the rink. Instead, he likes to twist, turn, and move. His family is upset because they think he is ruining hockey. One day, Henry watches figure skaters. They dance on the ice with music, spins, and special skates with picks. Henry wants to be an ice dancer, but Dad says no, and Sally says ice dancing is for girls. Henry stops skating. Then Grandma shows him a picture of herself as a young figure skater and gives him her old skates. Henry tries them and loves skating to music. Dad sees him and buys new figure skates. A coach begins teaching Henry. On his sixty-ninth try, Henry spins and finishes with one foot in the air. Grandma cheers for him.

video_title: 'Henry Holton Takes the Ice' read by Ray Romano

His family becomes upset, and Sally calls him a menace. One day, Henry watches figure skaters. He sees their spins and jumps and wants skates with picks on the blades. His dad refuses, and Sally says ice dancing is for girls, so Henry stops skating. Then Grandma shows Henry a picture of herself as a young figure skater. She gives him her old figure skates, and Henry returns to the ice. His dad sees him dance and buys him new figure skates. A coach begins teaching him. On his sixty-ninth try, Henry completes his special move, and Grandma proudly cheers for the new ice dancer.

video_title: 'A Tale of Two Beasts' read by Sarah Silverman

summaries.summary: While walking home from Grandma’s house through the deep dark woods, the narrator sees a strange little beast stuck in a tree. The beast cries, “Feep, feep, feep, feep,” so the narrator rescues him, names him Fang, wraps him in a scarf, and takes him home. Fang gets a bath, a hat, a sweater, fresh nuts, a house, and Lord Rex to play with. The narrator also takes him on long walkies and shows him to friends. However, Fang does not look happy and seems very hot. When the narrator opens a window, Fang throws off his clothes, jumps out, and runs back to the woods. The narrator cannot search because it is dinnertime, bathtime, and bedtime. Unable to sleep, the narrator misses Fang. Then Fang returns as a small furry shadow at the foot of the bed. He seems happy to see the narrator, who wonders why he came back.

video_title: 'A Tale of Two Beasts' read by Sarah Silverman

summaries.summary: The narrator was happily singing in a favorite tree when a terrible beast, saying “Growf!”, caught them. She tied them up and carried them to her secret lair. There, she made the narrator very clean, put on a silly hat and sweater, and offered squirrel food. The narrator did not like it. The beast kept them in a tiny box with nowhere to hang, made them walk backward and forward, and showed them to other wild beasts. The narrator had enough and made a clever plan: “a + b = freedom.” The plan worked, and the narrator escaped. They ran one mile back to the deep dark woods. The woods were quiet and wet, so the narrator wanted a warm hat. After dark, they sneaked back to get it. The terrible beast was waiting and seemed happy to see the narrator. Then the narrator wondered if she was not so terrible after all.

video_title: 'No More Noisy Nights' read by Tony Hale

summaries.summary: Jackson moved into a new house and went to bed at nine o’clock. During the night, he heard a loud OOOEEEeee sound from the attic. He thought a ghost was there, but the noise continued, so he used cotton balls in his ears. The next day, Jackson asked the ghost to stop. The ghost said it was sorry but did not know what else to do. Jackson placed a box in the attic. That night, he heard a BOOGETY WOOGETY sound from the basement. He asked the boogey monster to stop and left a box by the basement stairs. Then a pixie made Plink! Plink! sounds inside the piano. Jackson asked her to stop and put sheet music on the piano. That night, the ghost, monster, and pixie used the boxes, played music, and made quiet sounds. Jackson finally fell asleep with his new friends.

video_title: 'Rent Party Jazz' read by Viola Davis

summaries.summary: Every morning, Sonny worked for the coal man before going to school. He helped carry coal and earned ten cents a day. His Mama worked at a fish factory, but one day she lost her job. The rent was due, and the rent man would take their home if they could not pay. Mama told Sonny to stay in school while she looked for work. After school, Sonny watched Smilin’ Jack play his trumpet in Jackson Square. Sonny told him about their trouble. Smilin’ Jack explained how a rent party could raise money. Sonny invited the neighbors and found a bucket. That night, Smilin’ Jack played “Bourbon Street Rag,” and everyone ate, sang, clapped, and danced. People put coins in the bucket. The money paid the rent, and Smilin’ Jack gave the rest to people who needed food or rent money. Sonny stayed in school and learned that neighbors could help one another.

video_title: 'Rent Party Jazz' read by Viola Davis

Mama took enough for the rent, but Smilin’ Jack gave the rest to others who needed help. Sonny decided to remain in school and perhaps learn trumpet.

video_title: 'The House that Jane Built' read by Kiernan Shipka

summaries.summary: When Jane Addams was six, she saw poor people and wished to help fix the world. She grew up brave and smart, explored caves with her stepbrother George, and graduated first in her class at Rockford Female Seminary. After her father died, Jane felt lost. On a trip to London, she saw hungry people buying rotten food. At Toynbee Hall, she learned about settlement houses, where rich and poor people lived and learned together. Jane and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House in Chicago in 1889. Jane chose a poor neighborhood filled with garbage, crowded homes, and families who needed help. She left the door unlocked. People came for food, shoes, jobs, and other help. Jane started a public bath, Chicago’s first playground, kindergartens, clubs, and classes. She and other helpers taught English, art, cooking, and more. Hull House grew to thirteen buildings and helped thousands of people each week. Jane’s childhood wish came true.

video_title: 'The House that Jane Built' read by Kiernan Shipka

summaries.summary: When Jane Addams was six, she saw that some people lived in terrible conditions. She promised herself that she would someday live among poor families and help fix the world. Jane was brave and smart. She graduated first in her class from Rockford Female Seminary, but after her father died, she was unsure what to do. In London, she saw hungry people begging for spoiled food. Later, she visited Toynbee Hall, where rich and poor people lived together and learned useful skills. Jane decided to create a settlement house in Chicago with Ellen Gates Starr. In 1889, Jane moved into a house in a poor neighborhood. Helen Culver gave her the house, which Jane named Hull House. She left its doors unlocked so people could come for help. Hull House offered baths, a playground, kindergartens, clubs, classes, and jobs. Helpers joined Jane, and by 1907 Hull House had thirteen buildings. Thousands visited each week, and the community grew stronger.

video_title: 'The House that Jane Built' read by Kiernan Shipka

Seeing starving people in London led her to study Toynbee Hall, a settlement house where wealthy and poor people lived together and learned useful skills. Jane and Ellen Gates Starr opened Hull House in a house donated by Helen Culver. Jane left it unlocked so neighbors could enter for help. Hull House provided food, jobs, classes, baths, a playground, kindergarten, and clubs. Jane hired a burglar who admitted he needed work, and she convinced others to support her efforts. With many teachers and helpers, Hull House grew to thirteen buildings and served thousands each week. It transformed the neighborhood and helped inspire community centers across America.

video_title: 'As Fast As Words Could Fly' read by Dulé Hill

summaries.summary: Mason Steele lived in Greenville, North Carolina. He helped his father, Pa, with the civil rights group by writing letters about unfair treatment. The group gave Mason a typewriter, and he practiced every night. Mason and his brothers, Willis Jr. and Henry, then had to attend Belvoir High instead of the farther Bethel Union High. The white school bus first passed them, and later the driver made them sit in the back. At school, the principal and students treated them badly, but Mason worked hard. He got a library job typing book cards and became very fast. Mrs. Turner’s husband caused Mason to lose the job, but Pa and Golden Frinks helped him get it back. Mason won the chance to represent Belvoir High in a county typing tournament. He chose a manual typewriter and set a record of sixty-five words per minute. No one cheered, but Mason said the typewriter reminded him where he came from.

video_title: 'As Fast As Words Could Fly' read by Dulé Hill

summaries.summary: In Greenville, North Carolina, fourteen-year-old Mason Steele helps his father, Pa, with the civil rights group by turning meeting notes into letters. The group gives Mason a typewriter, and he practices after working in the tobacco fields. Mason and his brothers, Willis Jr. and Henry, then become the first Black students sent to nearby Belvoir High instead of a school twelve miles away. The bus driver refuses to stop for them for two days, and when they finally ride, they are sent to the back. At school, Principal Mr. Bullock and many students treat them badly, but Mason works hard and improves his typing. He gets a library job, but Mrs. Turner’s husband causes him to be fired because he is Black. Golden Frinks and Pa protest, and Mason is rehired. Mason wins Belvoir’s typing tournament spot and breaks the county record by typing sixty-five words per minute on a manual typewriter. He explains that it reminds him where he comes from.

video_title: 'Catching the Moon' read by Kevin Costner and Jillian Estell

summaries.summary: Marcenia Lyle loved baseball and dreamed of becoming a professional ballplayer. Her parents wanted her to think more about school and expected her to become a teacher, nurse, or maid. One day, Marcenia learned that Mr. Gabby Street was starting a free baseball camp, but he did not accept girls. Marcenia kept playing well. She caught balls, ran fast, scored runs, and hit a home run. In a close game, she stole home and scored the winning run. Mr. Street then invited her to camp, but she needed baseball cleats. Marcenia’s father said they could not buy any. The next day, Mr. Street gave Marcenia a pair of cleats because he wanted her in his camp. She played another great game in them. When her father saw the shoes, he agreed to take her to camp. Marcenia was happy because she was closer to making her dream come true.

video_title: 'The Tooth' read by Annette Bening

summaries.summary: Marissa loved candy, but one morning she woke with a toothache. Her mother took her downtown to the dentist instead of school. On the way, Marissa saw a quiet man with a large nose sitting on a sidewalk grate. An open shoebox in front of him held a little money. At the dentist’s office, Marissa watched people pass below while she waited. The dentist found a cavity and pulled out her tooth. He told her to brush twice a day, especially after eating candy. He put the tooth in a small orange envelope, and Marissa’s mother told her to place it under her pillow. Afterward, Marissa asked if there was a tooth fairy. Outside, the man was still sitting by the shoebox. Marissa dropped her tooth into it and told him to put it under his pillow so he would find money there the next day. The man smiled and waved goodbye. All he needed was a pillow.

video_title: 'To Be A Drum' read by James Earl Jones

summaries.summary: On a misty morning, Mat, Martha, and their daddy, Daddy Wes, sit in a field. Daddy Wes tells them how the first people in Africa heard the earth’s heartbeat and made the first drum. Later, men came, enslaved them, separated families, and took away their drums. Still, the earth’s spirit stayed inside the people. Their feet, mouths, hands, speech, courage, minds, communities, art, stories, history, work, and dreams became living drums. They stayed alive and would be free. Daddy Wes asks the children to listen to the earth. Martha hears its heartbeat, but Mat hears nothing. Daddy Wes tells Mat to be quiet and still. When Mat relaxes, he hears the heartbeat too. Daddy Wes asks what the earth says. Together, they drum its rhythm: “bum-bum, bum-bum, bum-bum.” Then they hold hands and leave the field. Daddy Wes says they will always know their own rhythm and can be free and become a drum.

video_title: 'To Be A Drum' read by James Earl Jones

Their feet, mouths, hands, minds, courage, communities, art, stories, history, and dreams became living drums. Daddy Wes says they would always be free. They leave holding hands, with the heartbeat sounding. “You, too, can be free. Become a drum.”

Later, enslavers captured them, separated families, forbade their languages, and took away their drums. However, the earth’s heartbeat continued through their bodies. They became “living drums,” using their feet, mouths, hands, minds, courage, communities, art, stories, history, and work to survive, create, and fight for freedom and civil rights. Together, they drum the rhythm: “bum-bum, bum-bum, bum-bum.” Daddy Wes says they can always make their own rhythm and tells them, “Become a drum.”

video_title: 'No Mirrors in My Nana's House' read by Tia & Tamera Mowry

summaries.summary: The narrator remembers staying at Nana’s house, where there were no mirrors. Because the narrator did not see a reflection, they did not know that people might think their skin was too black, their nose too flat, or their clothes did not fit. At Nana’s house, the narrator enjoyed everything. Cracks in the wall were interesting, dust was fun to taste and looked like snow in the sunlight, hallway noises sounded like music, and trash and rubbish softened the floor. Outside, the world seemed magical. The narrator knew love but did not know hate. Nana saw beauty in everything, and that beauty was in her eyes like the rising of the sun. The narrator tells the listener to look deeply into their eyes. The story then explains that the book was inspired by a song by Ysaye Barnwell, who was in Sweet Honey and the Rock. The song repeats the memories of Nana’s house and its beauty.

video_title: 'No Mirrors in My Nana's House' read by Tia & Tamera Mowry

summaries.summary: In Nana’s house, there were no mirrors. Because the child could not see a reflection, the child did not know that others might say their skin was too black, their nose was too flat, or their clothes did not fit. Instead, the child saw beauty in everything through Nana’s eyes, like the rising sun. The child enjoyed the cracks in the wall, tasted the dust that fell, heard noises in the hallway as music, and felt trash and rubbish cushion their feet. Outside, the world seemed magical because the child knew love and did not know hate. Throughout the song, the words repeat, “There were no mirrors in my Nana’s house.” The song ends with Nana’s instruction, “Chil’, look deep into my eyes.” The text also explains that the book was inspired by this song, which is performed by Ysaye Barnwell’s group, Sweet Honey and the Rock.

video_title: 'Romeow & Drooliet' read by Haylie Duff

summaries.summary: The Felinis were cat people who disliked dogs, and the Barkers were dog people who hated cats. One day, brothers Benny, Marky, and Romeow went to the park. Marky teased Turbo, a fierce dog, so the cats hurried away. That night, they went to the Barkers’ costume party. Romeow saw Drooliet, a beautiful dog, and they danced. They fell in love even though their families were enemies. Romeow jumped to Drooliet’s balcony, and they promised to marry. The next day, Mousignor Mouse married them. In the park, Turbo attacked Marky, and Romeow fought Turbo to protect his brother. Officer Prince then took Romeow to an animal control truck. Drooliet ran after him and was hit by a car. Romeow gave her one of his nine lives by licking her. Drooliet woke up, and everyone celebrated. The Felinis and Barkers became friends, and cats and dogs played together.

video_title: 'Romeow & Drooliet' read by Haylie Duff

summaries.summary: In a city where cats and dogs dislike each other, Felini brothers Benny, Marky, and Romeow visit the park. They secretly marry the next day with Mousignor Mouse. In the park, Turbo attacks Marky, and Romeow defeats him. Officer Prince then captures Romeow, believing Drooliet is the loose dog. Drooliet runs after the truck and is struck by a vehicle while crossing the street. Romeow finds her motionless and licks her, giving her one of his nine lives. Drooliet awakens, and everyone celebrates. The Barkers and Felinis become friends, Turbo, Benny, and Marky make peace, and Officer Prince drops the charges. Cats and dogs begin playing together, while Romeow and Drooliet share the rest of their lives.

video_title: 'Sebastian's Roller Skates' read by Caitlin Wachs

summaries.summary: Sebastian was very shy. He knew many things, but he usually looked down and said only, “Fine.” He knew geography, including the names of countries, seas, deserts, and capitals. Sebastian liked Ester, a girl in his class, but he had never spoken to her. One day, he found old roller skates in the park. At first, he fell again and again. He practiced every day, using trees, posts, and railings to help him. After a week, he still could not skate far. Then a big dog ran past and Sebastian grabbed its leash. The dog pulled him across the park, over a bridge, past the playground, and over a ditch. Sebastian learned that he could skate. He also began speaking more. He told the barber about deserts and said he did not want a billiard-ball haircut. He answered questions at school and asked Ester to skate with him. She said yes. Sebastian bought new skates and returned the old ones for someone else to find.

After that, Sebastian began speaking more confidently. He answered questions at school, told the barber what he wanted, and asked Ester to go skating. Ester said yes. Sebastian bought new skates and returned the old ones so someone else could learn too.

Afterward, Sebastian proudly told a neighbor that he was learning to roller skate. He also began speaking more confidently at the barbershop and school. Finally, he asked Ester to skate with him, and she agreed. Sebastian bought new skates, returned the old ones, and left them for someone else to find.

video_title: The Great Mouse Detective, 1986  Basil,

summaries.summary: On a stormy night in London, a bat with a peg leg and his helper, Fidget, kidnap the toy maker Hyram Flaversham from his shop. Hyram’s daughter, Olivia, meets Dr. Dawson, a mouse doctor, who takes her to Basil of Baker Street. Basil learns about the bat and starts the case. The kidnapper works for Professor Ratigan, who wants to rule all mice. Ratigan makes a mechanical copy of the mouse queen. Basil, Dawson, and Olivia find clues, but Fidget captures Olivia. Basil finds Ratigan’s hideout, but Ratigan captures Basil and Dawson and puts them in a dangerous trap. Basil escapes with Dawson. At the queen’s celebration, Ratigan uses the robot queen, but Basil and Dawson stop him. Olivia helps defeat Fidget. Ratigan grabs Olivia and runs to Big Ben. Basil saves Olivia, and Ratigan falls into the fog. Hyram and Olivia return home safely. Dawson stays to help Basil solve more cases.

video_title: The Great Mouse Detective, 1986  Basil,

Olivia meets Dr. Dawson, a mouse army surgeon, who takes her to Basil of Baker Street at 221 and a half Baker Street. Basil recognizes the clue and investigates. Fidget works for Professor Ratigan, who plans to rule all mice by using a mechanical copy of the mouse queen. Basil, Dawson, and Olivia find stolen tools and parts, but Fidget captures Olivia. Basil locates Ratigan’s sewer hideout, where he and Dawson are caught and placed in a complicated death trap. Basil studies the machine and escapes just in time. At Buckingham Palisaur, Ratigan uses the mechanical queen to claim power, but Basil takes control of it and exposes the plot. Ratigan kidnaps Olivia and flees to Big Ben. Basil rescues her, and Ratigan falls into the fog at midnight. Hyram is reunited with Olivia, and Dawson stays to become Basil’s partner.

video_title: Annie  1982

summaries.summary: In a cruel 1930s New York City orphanage, Miss Hanigan makes Annie and the other girls clean all day. Annie comforts them and hopes her real parents will return. The girls sing “It’s the Hard Knock Life,” but Annie runs away with her locket. She rescues a stray dog from dog catchers, names him Sandy, and is soon returned to the orphanage. Grace Frell then takes Annie to billionaire Oliver “Daddy” Warbucks’s mansion for Christmas. The servants welcome her, and Annie sings “I Think I’m Going to Like It Here.” Warbucks grows fond of Annie and promises to help find her parents. After he offers a reward, Miss Hanigan’s brother Rooster and his girlfriend, Lily St. Regis, pretend to be Annie’s parents. Annie goes with them, but Grace learns that Annie’s real parents died years earlier. Rooster and Lily take Annie to a bridge, where police and Warbucks rescue her. Rooster and Lily are captured, and Miss Hanigan is arrested. Warbucks adopts Annie, and she, Sandy, and the orphans celebrate by singing “Tomorrow.”

video_title: Annie  1982

Miss Hanigan is also arrested but forgiven by Annie. Warbucks adopts Annie, and the orphans join a joyful celebration.

video_title: The Night Is Short, Walk on Girl.

summaries.summary: At a wedding reception in Kyoto, a cheerful college sophomore known as the girl with black hair leaves to explore the endless night. Her classmate, Senpai, secretly follows her, hoping to meet her. At a hidden bar, she wins a drinking contest, even defeating Rihuku of the Pampacific Defensa. She then visits a used-book fair under a bridge and finds an old children’s book she once loved. Senpai tries to buy a rare book for her, but the collectors and constant interruptions stop him. At a gorilla theater performance, she joins the fun while Senpai’s attempts to confess become part of the comedy. During a freezing festival, she listens kindly to lonely and heartbroken people. Later, a cold epidemic makes many revelers sick, so she brings them food, tea, and comfort. She finds Senpai collapsed with a fever and realizes he has followed her all night. At dawn, they walk home together, exchange honest words, and begin a hopeful connection.

They walk home together, exchange sincere words, and begin a hopeful relationship.

video_title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, 1865 English children's novel by Lewis Carroll,

summaries.summary: Alice sits beside her sister when she sees a White Rabbit wearing a waistcoat and carrying a watch. She follows him into a rabbit hole and falls into Wonderland. In a hallway, she uses a small key, drinks a bottle, eats a cake, and changes sizes. She cries a pool of tears, then swims with a Mouse, a Dodo, and other animals. After a silly caucus race, Alice follows the Rabbit to his house, grows huge, and then returns to normal. In the woods, the Caterpillar gives her a mushroom that changes her size. The Cheshire Cat directs her to the Mad Hatter’s tea party, where the Hatter, March Hare, and Dormouse talk nonsense because it is always six o’clock. Alice meets the Queen of Hearts and plays chaotic croquet. She hears the Mock Turtle’s stories before attending a trial about the Queen’s stolen tarts. Alice grows tall, calls the court a pack of cards, and wakes beside her sister, realizing it was a dream.

video_title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, 1865 English children's novel by Lewis Carroll,

After shrinking again, she meets a mouse, a duck, a dodo, and other animals. They hold a pointless caucus race, then Alice follows the Rabbit to his house, where another potion makes her grow huge before a cake returns her to normal. In the forest, the Caterpillar gives her a mushroom that controls her size. The Cheshire Cat directs her to the Mad Hatter’s tea party. Alice later meets the Queen of Hearts, plays chaotic croquet, and hears the Mock Turtle’s stories. At a trial about stolen tarts, Alice grows tall and declares the court only a pack of cards. She wakes beside her sister and realizes Wonderland was a dream.

video_title: 5 Centimeters per Second

summaries.summary: In Tokyo in the early 1990s, quiet Takitoono and Akari become close friends. They share books, secrets, and time together, but Akari moves away. They continue writing letters until Takakei learns that his family will move to southern Japan. He travels by train to see Akari one last time, despite a dangerous snowstorm and long delays. She waits for him, and they share food, memories, and a kiss beneath a leafless cherry tree. However, the letter he wrote is blown away, and they soon separate. Years later, Takakei lives on Tanegashima, where Kana Sumida hopes to confess her love. She realizes that his heart still belongs to someone from his past and chooses to let go. As a programmer in Tokyo, Takakei remains lonely, while Akari prepares to marry and remembers their reunion fondly. At a railway crossing, Takakei thinks he sees Akari, but a train blocks her from view. He accepts the past and walks forward.

video_title: 5 Centimeters per Second

A passing train separates them, and Taki accepts the past before walking forward.

video_title: The Jungle Book

summaries.summary: Mali, also called Mowgli, is a man cub who grows up in the heart of the Indian jungle with wolves. His best friends are Bagira, a wise black panther, and Belaloo, a fun-loving bear. Mowgli spends his days having adventures, swinging on vines, swimming with his furry friends, and learning the bare necessities of life from Bulu. The jungle is his only home, and he thinks of himself as a bear. Then the dangerous tiger Shir Khan returns to the jungle. Because Shir Khan makes the jungle unsafe for Mowgli, Bagira and Baloo decide that Mowgli must leave. They try to take him to the man village, where humans live. This is difficult because Mowgli does not want to leave his animal friends or the jungle. Bagira and Baloo continue helping him as they try to show him where he belongs. Their journey is sometimes funny, sometimes difficult, and heartwarming.

video_title: Kiki's Delivery Service

summaries.summary: When Kiki turns 13, witch tradition requires her to leave home and live alone in a new town for one year. She flies away on a broomstick with her talking black cat, Gigi, and settles in Kurik, a busy port city. After Kiki returns a customer’s pacifier, Osono, the kind bakery owner, gives her a room in exchange for help. Kiki then starts a witch’s delivery service. She delivers a stuffed cat toy to a boy’s party and carries herring and pumpkin pie to a granddaughter. She also meets Tombbo, a boy who loves airplanes. Soon, work and self-doubt cause Kiki to lose her magic. She cannot control her broom or understand Gigi. Kiki visits Ursula, an artist, who says that creativity and magic need time to rest. When Tombbo is endangered by an airship in a storm, Kiki uses a street sweeper’s broom and regains her magic to rescue him. The city celebrates Kiki, and she continues her deliveries with confidence.

video_title: My Neighbor Totoro

summaries.summary: Satsuki and her younger sister, May Kusa, leave the busy streets of Tokyo and move to a quiet home in the countryside. They move so they can be closer to their mother, who is in the hospital. While exploring their new home and the woods around it, the sisters discover wondrous forest spirits called the Kodama. One day, May meets a giant, furry creature named Todoro. Although Todoro is very large, he is gentle and enjoys playing with the girls. Todoro and his friends take Satsuki and May on magical adventures. As the sisters spend time with the forest spirits, they learn about the natural world and the importance of family and friendship. Their mother stays in the hospital while she recovers. Satsuki and May continue to enjoy their adventures with Todoro and his friends, and they remain cheerful while they wait for their mother to get better.

video_title: Sweet Porridge   Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm

summaries.summary: A poor but good little girl lived alone with her mother, and they had no food left. The girl went into the forest, where an aged woman heard about her sorrow and gave her a little pot. When the girl said, “Cook, little pot, cook,” it made good, sweet porridge. When she said, “Stop, little pot,” it stopped. The girl took it home, so she and her mother no longer went hungry. One day, while the girl was away, her mother told the pot to cook. She ate until she was full, but she did not know the words to make it stop. The porridge filled the kitchen, the house, the next house, and the whole street. No one could stop it. When the girl returned, only one house was still empty. She said, “Stop, little pot,” and the pot stopped cooking. Anyone returning to town had to eat through the porridge.

video_title: Neon Genesis Evangelion  The End of Evangelion J

summaries.summary: Shinji, Rey, and Asuka are trapped inside the giant Ava unit Z01 until Kawaru rescues them. With his help, Shinji repairs Ava Z01, and they escape Nerve’s collapsing headquarters. Misato and Ritsuko pick them up in a submarine, but during an argument, Shinji and the other two Avas are forced deep into the ocean. At a trench more than seven miles down, they find a huge black sphere. As they approach it, their bodies break down, and they become infants without their memories. A flashback reveals that Gendo had been working with Seal. Gendo plans to use Adam’s core and Lilith’s core to begin the human instrumentality project, which would destroy and remake humanity. He enters Ava01, but Yui, Shinji’s mother, asks him to stop. Gendo refuses, so the project begins and the world is consumed. Later, Gendo apologizes to Yui, and both disappear into light. At the end, Shinji, Rey, and Asuka play on a beach.

video_title: Sleeping Beauty - Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm

summaries.summary: A king and queen longed for a child. A frog told the queen she would have a daughter, and soon Princess Rosamund was born. The king held a great feast and invited twelve wise women, but left out the thirteenth because there were only twelve golden plates. The wise women gave Rosamund wonderful gifts. The angry thirteenth woman cursed her to prick her finger on a spindle at age fifteen and die. The twelfth woman softened the curse: Rosamund would sleep for one hundred years. The king ordered all spindles burned. On her fifteenth birthday, Rosamund found an old woman spinning in a tower and pricked her finger. She and everyone in the castle fell asleep, while a hedge of thorns grew around it. After one hundred years, a prince entered when the thorns became flowers. He kissed Rosamund, and she awoke. The castle woke too, and Rosamund and the prince were married and lived happily together.

video_title: Greek myths, Medusa

summaries.summary: Medusa was one of three Gorgon sisters. Her sisters, Theo and Uri, were immortal, but Medusa was mortal. Her parents were Fors and Sat, ancient sea gods. Medusa was once a beautiful maiden with lovely hair. In the myth, she was changed after boasting about her beauty or after Poseidon harmed her in Athena’s temple. Athena became angry and turned Medusa into a monster. Snakes grew from her hair, and anyone who looked at her eyes turned to stone. The hero Perseus was sent to kill her. Athena and Hermes helped him. Perseus used a bronze shield to see Medusa’s reflection, so he did not look at her directly. While Medusa slept, he cut off her head. Pegasus, a winged horse, and Chrysair sprang from her blood. Perseus gave Medusa’s head to Athena, who put it on her shield, the Aegis. Her image was later used on armor and buildings for protection.

video_title: Greek myths, Medusa

summaries.summary: Medusa was one of three Gorgon sisters, along with Theo and Uri. Unlike her sisters, she was mortal and could die. Her parents were Fors and Sat, primordial sea gods. Medusa was once a beautiful maiden admired for her hair. In different versions of the myth, she either boasted about her beauty or was violated by Poseidon in Athena’s temple. Athena became angry and transformed Medusa into a monster with snakes for hair. Anyone who looked directly at her turned to stone. The hero Perseus was sent to kill her. Athena and Hermes helped him, and he used a bronze shield to see Medusa’s reflection without meeting her gaze. He found her sleeping and cut off her head. Pegasus, the winged horse, and Chrysair sprang from her blood; they were Medusa’s children by Poseidon. Perseus gave her head to Athena, who placed it on her shield, the Aegis. Medusa’s image later appeared on armor and buildings as protection against evil, and her story received different interpretations.

video_title: The Dragon and His Grandmother,

summaries.summary: Three soldiers ran away from the army because their pay was too small. They hid in a cornfield, but the army stayed nearby. After two days, they were hungry and feared being hanged. A fiery dragon offered to save them if they served him for seven years. He gave them a little whip that made money appear, and they signed his book. The soldiers lived richly for seven years. As the time ended, two became afraid, but the third soldier stayed brave. An old woman told him to visit a rock hut in the wood. There, the dragon’s grandmother hid him under a stone. She heard the dragon tell three riddles: a person, a bell, and one man going to St. Ives. The soldier remembered the answers and told his friends. After seven years, the dragon asked the riddles. The soldiers answered correctly, so the dragon flew away, and they were free. They used the whip and lived happily.

video_title: Your Name is no exception

summaries.summary: The film follows Taki Takachi Bana, a teenage boy in Tokyo, and Mizuami Ameia, a teenage girl living in the countryside with her grandmother and little sister. Though they have never met, they feel strongly connected and discover that they swap bodies whenever they fall asleep. At first, they enjoy experiencing each other’s lives, but losing control of their bodies soon causes problems. They agree to meet in person and solve the mystery. When the boy is in Mizuami’s body, he takes it to Tokyo, planning to return it the next day. However, her little sister becomes sick, so he cares for her. Mizuami’s grandmother grows suspicious and threatens to call the police, forcing him to escape. He meets a friend, then attends a fireworks festival. Meanwhile, Mizuami returns to her body and finds a blue umbrella left by him. She travels to Tokyo to find him, but he has disappeared, leaving her with the umbrella and memories.

video_title: Tick Tock Turkey and the Disappearing Sandwich

summaries.summary: Tick Tock Turkey and Future Dog live on Egg Island and can travel through time with a special watch. One morning, Tick Tock Turkey makes what he believes is the best sandwich ever. He gathers crusty bread, butter, orange lettuce, blue tomatoes, a yellow onion, purple cheese, mustard, pink gravy, and hot chocolate sauce. When the sandwich is ready, he asks Future Dog to look at it. Two loud whooshes sound, and the sandwich suddenly disappears. Tick Tock Turkey decides to use his watch. He turns it back two minutes and opens a time hole. Then he jumps through and brings the sandwich back before the thief can take it. Future Dog explains that the thief was a future Tick Tock Turkey who came back for the sandwich. Tick Tock Turkey is confused because he took the sandwich from himself. Finally, he eats it and agrees that it is the best sandwich ever.

video_title: The frog prince

summaries.summary: A beautiful princess often played with her golden ball beside a forest well. One day, the ball rolled into the deep water, and she began to cry. A frog offered to get it if she promised to let him be her companion, eat at her table, and sleep in her bed. She agreed, but after the frog returned the ball, she ran home and forgot him. The next day, the frog came to the castle. The king told his daughter to keep her promise, so she let the frog eat with her and follow her to bed, although she disliked him. When he asked her to lift him, she angrily threw him against a wall. The frog became a kind prince who had been bewitched by a wicked witch. He and the princess were to marry and travel to his kingdom. Faithful Henry carried them in a carriage, and bands around his heart broke with joy when the prince was freed.

The narrator thought Hawaii was beautiful and wanted to go back.

summaries.summary: It is a quiet afternoon on a farm. The horse swishes his tail, the cow chews, the pig plays in mud, and the sheep eats grass. Suddenly, a duck shouts, “Duck!” The horse says the duck is small and waddly, while he is tall and noble. The cow says the duck has webbed feet, but she has hooves. The pig says the duck has a beak, but he has a snout. The sheep says the duck has feathers, but she has wool. Each animal says that everyone is different. Some are ducks, and most are not. They tell the duck to stop shouting and say it is rude to run around calling out his name. The duck apologizes and says he should have said something else. Then he shouts, “RUN!” The horse, cow, pig, and sheep learn that the duck’s cries were warnings, and they run away.

One day, the wizard Merlin arrives and uses magic to make it snow, so Sir Ector allows him to teach Wart. Merlin changes Wart into a fish, and Wart hides from a large fish by using his head. As a squirrel, he learns to prepare for tomorrow, and as a bird, he sees the world from above and becomes wiser. Later, a knight announces a tournament in London to choose England’s king. Kay and Wart travel there, but Wart forgets Kay’s sword. In a churchyard, Wart pulls a sword from an anvil and carries it back. Golden letters say that whoever removes the sword is the rightful king of England. Nobody else can pull it out, proving Wart is chosen. His lessons prepared him, and he becomes King Arthur.

The child also realizes that some activities are neither fun nor boring, such as brushing teeth, riding the bus, and waiting for a light. Grandpa enjoys telling stories about boring experiences, so the child wonders if boring things become fun later. Dad says being an adult can be boring, but people can make things fun. The child draws a maze, then says Dad's idea is boring because it has been heard before.

She asked him to deliver a message wishing the king and queen a merry Christmas and peaceful new year. The coals grew hotter on the journey back. The servant relit the fire, and its warmth spread through the castle. The king and queen reunited, and warmth reached the valley, thawing even the grumpy people's hearts because kindness spreads more kindness.

video_title: The Warm Glow

summaries.summary: In a green valley, an elderly king and queen live alone in a castle with a few servants. Each night they sit by the kitchen fire, but one evening they argue and separate. The fire goes out, and the servants cannot relight it. Cold spreads through the castle and valley during the winter festivities. The king sends a servant with a lantern and gold coins to collect six hot coals. A grumpy man and then a grumpy woman each sell him six coals for 12 gold coins, but both times the coals turn black after five steps. At the third cottage, a kind woman welcomes the servant, gives him hot turnip soup, and offers six coals without payment. She asks him to deliver a Christmas and New Year message to the king and queen. The coals remain hot, so the servant relights the castle fire. Its warmth melts the couple’s disagreement and spreads through the valley, thawing even the grumpy people’s hearts.

video_title: Māui and the Giant Fish

summaries.summary: Long ago, Maui was a clever trickster demigod. His older brothers would not let him fish with them because they thought he was too small. Maui wanted to prove he was a good fisherman, so he secretly made a strong fishing line, said a magical kakia, and attached a jawbone from his ancestor Moodyangua as a hook. He hid in his brothers’ waka, or canoe, and surprised them far out at sea. Maui said a katakia, and the brothers caught many fish. Then Maui used his own line and his blood for bait. His hook reached Tangar, the god of the sea, and caught a huge fish. Maui pulled it up and asked his brothers to guard it while he fetched their people. Instead, they chopped pieces from it. The cuts became the hills, valleys, and mountains of New Zealand. The fish became Teika Amawi, the North Island, and their waka became Twaka a Maui, the South Island.

video_title: Why Anansi has Long, Thin Legs

summaries.summary: Emily tells about Anancy, a greedy, lazy spider whose eight legs are short. One day, Anancy smells delicious food at Rabbit’s house. Rabbit is cooking green beans and invites him to lunch. When Rabbit asks him to help lay the table, Anancy ties a thread from the pot to his leg and leaves. He does the same at Monkey’s house with sweet potato, Tiger’s house with oine, and Lizard’s house with pumpkin. He also visits Elephant, Turtle, Zebra, and Parrot, tying a thread to each cooking pot. Soon, all eight meals are ready. The animals pull their threads at the same time. Anancy is pulled in many directions, so hard that his legs stretch long and thin. The threads snap, and Anancy falls into the river. He climbs out cold, wet, and hungry. From then on, Anancy has eight long, spindly legs and helps lay the table when invited to lunch.

video_title: Why Anansi has Long, Thin Legs

He did the same at Monkey’s house with sweet potatoes and at Tiger’s house with oine. Then he visited Lizard, who was cooking pumpkin, and also Elephant, Turtle, Zebra, and Parrot. At every house, Anancy tied another thread to a pot and one of his legs, planning to eat all eight lunches. When the food was ready, all the animals pulled their threads. Anancy was yanked in many directions, so hard that his legs stretched longer and thinner. The threads snapped, and he landed in the river. He climbed out wet, cold, and hungry. From then on, spiders had long, spindly legs, and Anancy helped lay the table when invited to lunch.

video_title: Goanna and The Fairies

summaries.summary: Deep in an Australian forest, fairies woke up and made wattleseed damper for their feast. They ground wattleseed between rocks, mixed it with flower petals and morning dew, and hid the dough under a tree root. Guana watched and waited until the fairies slept. Then he ate the dough, basket and all. The fairies were sad, so a little fairy and her brother went to a human camp. They brought back two fiery red chilies. The grandmother fairies chopped the chilies and mixed them into new damper. This time, the fairies hid and watched Guana. He ate the spicy damper and ran to the creek. He drank so much water that his belly became very full. When he tried to run away, he could hardly move. Guana was never seen there again. The fairies feasted and danced. The story also says that Earth is our mother and we must take care of her.

video_title: Goanna and The Fairies

summaries.summary: In an Australian forest clearing, fairies wake to celebrate the wattle season and thank Mother Earth. They grind wattle seeds between rocks, mix the flour with flower petals and morning dew, knead the dough, and hide it under a tree root to rise. Guana watches, waits until they sleep, and gobbles the damper and basket. The next day, the fairies are upset, so a little fairy and her brother volunteer to visit a human camp. They bring back two fiery red chilies from a basket. Grandmother fairies chop the chilies and mix them into new damper dough. The fairies hide and watch as Guana eats it. The spicy damper makes him run in circles and drink nearly all the water in the creek. When the fairies ask why he steals instead of asking for a share, Guana tries to chase them, but his water-filled belly makes him leave. He is never seen there again, and the fairies feast and dance.

video_title: How Otter Tricked Rabbit

summaries.summary: In the beginning, all animals spoke the same language. They had games, dances, and a tribal council. Rabbit talked too much and loved playing tricks, so he became the council messenger. First, the animals held a flying contest. Bat hid in Eagle’s feathers, but Eagle won, and the animals held an honor dance for him. Next, they chose Otter for having the prettiest fur. Rabbit felt jealous. While taking Otter to the dance, Rabbit tricked him. He threw fire coals into the air and told Otter to jump into the river. Otter did, and Rabbit stole his fur coat. At the dance, Rabbit wore the coat and covered his nose and ears. Bear noticed that he was not acting like Otter. Bear knocked Rabbit’s paw away, and everyone saw Rabbit’s nose. Rabbit ran, but Bear pulled off his long tail. That is why rabbits have short, fluffy tails. Otter got his coat back and discovered that he loved swimming, so otters have lived in water ever since.

video_title: How Otter Tricked Rabbit

summaries.summary: Long ago, animals spoke the same language and held contests and dances. Rabbit talked a lot, played tricks, and served as the animal council’s messenger. In a flying contest, Eagle won, so the animals honored him with a dance. Next, they chose Otter for having the prettiest fur coat. Rabbit felt jealous. While taking Otter to the council house, Rabbit invented a story about fire falling from the sky. He told Otter to sleep by the river and hang his coat in a tree. When Otter slept, Rabbit threw hot coals into the air. Otter jumped into the river, and Rabbit stole his coat. Rabbit tied down his ears, wore the coat, and led the dance with a paw over his nose. Bear noticed that he was acting strangely and knocked away the paw. Everyone saw Rabbit, and Bear pulled off Rabbit’s long tail. Otter got his coat back and discovered that he loved swimming. Since then, otters have lived in water, and rabbits have only small, puffy tails.

video_title: How Otter Tricked Rabbit

summaries.summary: In the beginning, animals spoke one language, held councils, played games, and loved to dance. Rabbit was the council messenger because he talked constantly, but he also loved tricks. When Eagle won a contest for flying highest, the animals held an honor dance. Then they chose Otter, whose thick, rich fur was the prettiest, to lead the next dance. Rabbit felt jealous of Otter and his own bushy tail. While taking Otter the message, Rabbit tricked him by inventing a place where fire supposedly fell from the sky. Otter removed his coat and slept beside the river. Rabbit threw hot coals into the air, frightened Otter into the water, and stole the coat. At the dance, Rabbit disguised himself as Otter and covered his split nose with a paw. Bear suspected him, knocked the paw away, and exposed Rabbit. Rabbit fled, but Bear pulled off his long tail. Otter got his coat back and discovered he loved swimming, so otters have lived in water ever since.

video_title: Anansi and the Magic Yams

summaries.summary: Nancy the Spider had a field full of ripe yams, but he was lazy and did not want to dig them up. He asked his friend Brother Tiger to do the work and promised him half the yams. Brother Tiger dug and pulled, but each yam went farther into the ground. He became tired and angry and gave a loud roar. Then the strange yams climbed out of the soil. They had legs, arms, and eyes, and they chased Brother Tiger while saying, “boom boom.” Brother Tiger hid in Brother Dog’s house and then Sister Duck’s house, but his loud roars showed the yams where he was. He ran to Brother Goat, who led him across a log over the river. Brother Goat knocked the yams into the water with his horns. The animals later made a yam feast. Brother Tiger never trusted Nancy the Spider again, and “boom boom” frightened him.

video_title: Anansi and the Magic Yams

Tiger ran to Brother Goat, who led him across a river on a log. Goat stayed behind and knocked the yams into the water with his horns. The yams stopped chasing Tiger. Tiger and Goat gathered them and planned a yam feast. Tiger blamed Nancy the Spider and never trusted Nancy again. The “boom boom” sound frightened Tiger from then on.

video_title: The Devil and the Boy Who Knew How to Read

summaries.summary: A poor boy leaves his small village in the desert of northern Mexico to find work. He meets a rich man dressed in black, who offers him a job if he cannot read. The boy tricks him by pretending to have a twin brother who cannot read. He changes his clothes and meets the man again. The man takes him through a magic rock into an underground mansion filled with dusty books. At night, the boy discovers that the man is El Diablo, the Devil. He secretly reads books of magic and learns spells that make the house clean itself. After reading every book, he becomes wise and powerful. One day, El Diablo catches him reading. The boy changes into a mouse, a dove, and a turtle to escape. El Diablo changes into a cat, a hawk, and then a leaf. The turtle eats the leaf because the boy knows it is El Diablo. The boy becomes himself again and lets El Diablo out through the toilet.

video_title: The Devil and the Boy Who Knew How to Read

The boy tricks him by pretending to be his illiterate twin. He changes his clothes and appearance, then meets the man again. They travel underground through a magical rock to a huge mansion filled with dusty books. At night, the boy discovers that the man is El Diablo, a powerful devil. To protect himself, he secretly studies magic and learns spells that make the housework happen. After reading every book, he becomes a skilled magician. One morning, the devil catches him reading, so the boy changes into a mouse, dove, and turtle while escaping. The devil becomes a cat, hawk, and leaf. The boy recognizes the leaf, eats it, changes back, and lets the devil out through the toilet.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - Gulbahar

summaries.summary: Mara was a poor woman who lived with her husband and baby daughter. One day, she found good figs in an old palace garden. When she touched a fig, a scary witch appeared and demanded one hundred gold coins. Mara had no coins, so the witch said she would take the baby. Mara fainted, but the witch disappeared. Years later, Mara’s daughter, Gulbahar, touched a butterfly with the same marks as the witch and was taken to the palace. The witch made Gulbahar knit and gave her rice and figs. She told Gulbahar not to open a chest, look in a mirror, or look outside. Gulbahar did all three. The mirror told her that three balls of wool held the witch’s power. After seven years, a prince came to help her. They escaped using sheets and took the balls of wool. The green ball made brambles, the blue ball made a lake, and the red ball made a fire that destroyed the witch. Gulbahar married the prince, and her parents came to live with them.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - Gulbahar

summaries.summary: In Iran, Mara was poor and gathered herbs and figs for her family. When she touched a fig in a ruined palace garden, a witch appeared. Mara had no money, so the witch claimed Mara’s baby daughter as payment. The witch vanished, and years passed. Mara’s daughter Gulbahar grew beautiful. While chasing a marked butterfly, Gulbahar was captured and taken to the palace. The witch made her knit and warned her not to open a chest, look in a mirror, or look outside. Gulbahar opened the chest and looked in the mirror. She learned that three wool balls held the witch’s power. After seven years, a prince climbed to her room. She hid him as a shawl, then changed him back. They escaped down tied sheets with the wool balls. The green ball grew thorny brambles, the blue made a lake, and the red made fire that destroyed the witch. Gulbahar and the prince married, and her parents came to live with them in the palace.

The witch chased them, but green wool made brambles, blue made a lake, and red made fire that destroyed her. Gulbahar and the prince reached his kingdom, and her parents joined them in the palace.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - The Griffin

summaries.summary: In Ireland, a rich man’s wife died, and soon his only son became very sick. A quack doctor said three fresh feathers from a griffin’s tail could cure him. Jack, a poor farmer’s son, agreed to find them. On his journey, a family asked him to learn why their daughter sat in a trance. An old farmer asked where his lost chest key was, and a ferryman asked why he could never leave his boat. Jack reached the griffin’s castle and hid in a cupboard. The griffin’s wife pulled three feathers from his tail and asked about the three problems. The griffin said the girl needed a lock of hair from a swallow’s nest, the key was in a crack in the farmer’s kitchen floor, and the ferryman could leave by giving his oars to the next passenger. Jack helped everyone. Then he used the feathers to cure the boy. The rich man gave Jack land and a house.

video_title: Bouki Dances The Kokioko

summaries.summary: Long ago in Haiti, a king loved dancing and welcomed entertainers to his palace. His treasurer, Malice, told him the kingdom had very few cowrie shells left, so the king could not pay performers anymore. The king then made up a song and dance called “Kokiyoko samba” and announced a contest. Whoever could perform it would win 100,000 cowrie shells. Dancers came from many places, but the king said none had danced it correctly. Malice secretly watched the king practice and wrote down the words and steps. Because Malice worked for the king, he asked his friend Buki to enter the contest. After much practice, Buki learned the dance. At the palace, Buki performed it perfectly and won the prize. On the way home, Malice tricked Buki into dancing with his eyes closed, then stole the sack of cowrie shells. Buki became dizzy, fell down, and returned home without the prize.

Buki returned home with nothing, saying Malice had fooled him again.

Since he could not compete as the king’s treasurer, Malice taught them to his friend Buki, a hardworking farmer. Buki performed the dance correctly and won the prize. video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - Ted the Tiger Tamer

summaries.summary: Ted discovers that he can turn into a huge tiger. At school, Rosie tries to take his tiger drawing, so Ted’s tiger roars and grows bigger. Ted pushes Rosie away, runs outside, and climbs an oak tree. His teacher, Mrs Mcintosh, makes him sit in the thinking chair. On the way home, Ted tells Gran what happened. Gran says everyone has a tiger inside and teaches Ted how to tame his: stop, breathe slowly, and say his tiger rhyme. Ted practices when his little sister takes his orange pen, and he sends the tiger away. On Sunday, Dad does not come to take Ted to the park. Ted becomes angry, and his tiger appears again. Ted runs through the rain until he reaches a bus shelter. He turns it into a cage, then uses breathing, his rhyme, and strong commands to make the tiger sit and go away. Dad finds Ted and carries him home. Ted learns to stop, breathe, and send his tiger away.

video_title: The Fearsome Creature in the House

summaries.summary: Hare lived in a little house at the bottom of a tree. One morning, she came home from her run and heard a loud voice say, “Go away!” The voice claimed to be long, eat trees, and trample elephants, so Hare was afraid and cried outside. Jackal, Monkey, Woodpecker, Snake, and Elephant each tried to help, but their plans could damage Hare’s door, roof, windows, or house. They all became frightened and left. Then a tiny tree frog came along. Frog found a gap under the door and quietly slipped inside. Soon Frog called, “Rabbit rabbit! You can come in now.” Hare entered and saw a big iron cooking pot. A caterpillar sat on its rim, making the booming voice. Frog told the caterpillar that he ate caterpillars, then jumped on it and ate it. Frog left, and Hare could make her breakfast peacefully in her house.

video_title: The Fearsome Creature in the House

Jackal, Monkey, Woodpecker, Snake, and Elephant each came to help, but their plans would damage the house: breaking the door, removing the roof tiles, breaking the windows, or lighting a fire. Elephant became frightened and ran away. At last, a tiny tree frog arrived and quietly squeezed under the door. He told Hare to enter, and she found a caterpillar sitting on her cooking pot. The pot had made the caterpillar’s voice sound large and frightening. The frog then pretended to be a creature that ate caterpillars. The surprised caterpillar fell from the pot, and the frog ate her. Hare could finally return inside and make her breakfast in peace.

summaries.summary: On Christmas Day, Joe feels unhappy. It is raining instead of snowing, Nan and Grandad cannot come, Dad is cooking sprouts, Rosie scribbled in his dinosaur book, and Mum makes him wear a Christmas jumper he dislikes. Joe, Rosie, and John ride the sledge together in the snow. Joe’s Christmas becomes happy because he shares.

video_title: Read Aloud- Give a Goat By: Jan West Schrock

summaries.summary: On a rainy day, Mrs. Raul read Beatrice’s Goat to her fifth-grade class. Beatrice lived in Uganda and could not attend school because her family had little money. When her mother received a goat, the family had plenty of milk to drink and sell. The money helped Beatrice go to school. Inspired by the story, the class decided to raise $120 for a goat. Ralph and the narrator learned from Miss Basinger about Heifer International and its idea of “passing on the gift,” when an animal’s baby is given to another family. With Mrs. Raul’s $15 loan, the students bought nuts, popcorn, and raisins, packaged them, kept records, and sold healthy snacks to teachers, children, and families. They repaid the loan and earned $180, enough to buy a goat, chickens, and ducks for three families. Other classes also raised money for charity. The students learned that one gift can help many families.

video_title: The Boy With The Rainbow Heart (Children’s Book Read Aloud)

summaries.summary: There was a boy with a rainbow heart. He lived in the town of gray. Everything he touched filled with colorful rays, but the town was sad and dark. The people were afraid of hearts that looked different from theirs. The boy stayed happy, and his bright heart kept shining. Each day, he wore his colors on his sleeves. His rays spread through the town, and the gray began to go away. Yellow came first, then blue, red, and green. Soon the town shined with many colors. Black faded, and gray followed, until the whole town was under a rainbow. The people’s hearts changed too. As each new color appeared, their fears fell apart. The boy’s love for all people changed their hearts, and they understood. In the new town of shine, the boy lived a great life. The story says that a heart with true love is always perfect when it is kind.

video_title: The World's Worst Teachers - Miss Spick's Trike of Terror

Soon, the children stopped visiting the library because Miss SPI took all their money. Only the clever Tang twins, Tom and Tim, always returned books perfectly clean. One day, Miss SPI fined them for a burger wrapper, even though it had blown next to them. As she rode away, the twins saw that a flap on her scooter was dropping litter. They made a plan. After reading about rockets, they secretly attached two booster rockets to the Trike of Terror. During break time, Miss SPI started her scooter. The rockets fired and sent her high into the sky. The rockets fell back with parachutes, but Miss SPI and her scooter floated in space, where pieces of old spacecraft bumped into them. Tom and Tim stayed at school and celebrated their plan.

Miss Seve thought she would retire, but Miss Stint said she would stay for another 50 years. Miss Seve became furious and gave Miss Stint, Miss Epoch, and everyone at the party a detention. She sent more than 1,000 people into her small classroom. Then she gave herself a detention too. While making everyone write lines, she spun her walking stick so fast that she flew through the roof. The school returned to the party, but nobody knew where Miss Seve landed.

video_title: The World's Worst Teachers - Miss Palaver's Theatrical Theatrics

summaries.summary: Miss Palava was a drama teacher at Lady Ostentatious School for Posh Girls. She turned every small event into a huge performance and spoke like William Shakespeare. She wore old-fashioned clothes and loved directing long, strange plays. Her productions included a 17-hour history of the world, a musical about her goldfish, a play about her own life, and an opera about biscuits fighting in Biscuit Tinland. Every girl had to act in her plays, and rehearsals often lasted for months or years. One day, the head mistress told Miss Palava that the school would have no more plays. The girls wanted the theater changed into a badminton room because the plays caused misery. Miss Palava was shocked and began to wail. Her loud crying broke windows, shook the building, and made the old school collapse. Everyone escaped to the lawn. When the dust cleared, Miss Palava stood in the rubble and asked if she could direct 36 of Shakespeare’s plays instead.

video_title: The World's Worst Teachers - Miss Conceit, the Human Work of Art

When she hears about the Nationwide Children’s Art Contest, or CAC, she decides the school’s artwork must be a giant sculpture of her. The children work for months, but Miss Conceit rejects everything because it is not beautiful enough. Alexina, the naughtiest pupil, makes a secret plan. She tells Miss Conceit that the sculpture will look better if the teacher herself is its base. Proudly, Miss Conceit squats down, and the children cover her with paper and paste. They make the statue huge and paint her face with a strained expression. The statue is sent to the Great and Good Art Gallery, or Gaga, and wins the contest. Miss Conceit remains trapped inside it for years, still calling for help.

Walter competed against Fuma the Fumer, who thumped people, and Pierre Leo, whose awful cheese burps made people sick. In the final events, Walter made a shy teacher cry and won. Walter cried, and Otto won the trophy, then smashed it because bullying belongs in the bin.

He put up posters asking for “pretty girls only.” Emiline, the smartest girl, made a secret plan with the other girls. On Friday, 342 girls met Valentine and Miss Pankhurst, the world-record official. The girls wore masks made from Valentine’s posters, so they all looked like him. When the chase began, Valentine ran away, but he stopped to admire his reflection in a puddle. The girls caught him and accidentally flattened him. Valentine stood up as wide as a house and looked very strange, but he was happy because he thought he would be famous. The girls laughed as he floated away like a kite.

Tom turns yellow and shiny like ear wax, Dick turns green and sticky like a bogey, and Harry becomes a giant ball of fluff. The next morning, they see what has happened and cry for help. Their mother takes them to school anyway. The children there laugh at Tom, Dick, and Harry, just as the triplets had laughed at other people. She dressed in pajamas, tied a black sock on her head, and used kung fu to hurt three school bullies, her teachers, the dinner lady, her family, and even the cat. Soon, people in Dollop called her Kung Fu Kylie, and PC Shod recorded 3,177 incidents. She damaged shops, vehicles, buildings, and other things, so Mayor Plunk called a town meeting. When Kylie attacked the Town Square, Raj tried to face her but ran away. He hit a tree and fell unconscious. Mrs Tog fell from the tree onto Kylie, stopping her. Kylie promised to stop using kung fu. video_title: The World's Worst Children 3 - Tandy's Tantrums

summaries.summary: Tandy had tantrums from babyhood. Because grown-ups always gave her what she wanted, her tantrums became louder and happened many times each day. When her parents offered fruit instead of ice cream, Tandy screamed, spat out grapes and bananas, and made the house shake. Her parents gave her a huge bowl of ice cream with flakes and chocolate sauce. Father then got noise-cancelling headphones for himself and Mother. When Tandy demanded dinner, they kept reading until she said “please.” Tandy decided her tantrums had to become louder. Tandy began having a tantrum about her spoiled tantrum. Mother and Father decided to move to Australia. They left Tandy behind, and no one was there to run to her when she had more tantrums.
